name: Iceland
subtitle: Iceland is not an EU member. It sits in this project as a control — one of the comparison countries every estimate is measured against. Applied in 2009 after the banking collapse, suspended talks in 2013, and holds an advisory referendum on resuming them on 29 August 2026. The vertical line marks entry into the European Economic Area on 1 January 1994: the single market without the Union.

kpis.label: GNI per capita (PPP), vs EU average
kpis.delta: World Bank · not a member, shown against the EU average

kpis.label: Trade openness
kpis.delta: exports + imports, % of GDP · World Bank

heroChart.title: Income relative to the EU average
heroChart.sub: GNI per capita at purchasing-power parity as a share of the EU-wide average. GNI rather than GDP, because GDP overstates income in economies where a lot of output accrues to non-residents. The 2008 collapse is the largest single movement on this page: 128% of the EU average in 2007, 104% by 2010. Iceland's EU application followed it by nine months, and the application was suspended once the economy had recovered — which is why this country's position on membership is hard to read off its income line.

legal.title: Legal
paras: Iceland is not bound by the EU treaties, and is bound by a great deal of EU law anyway. The EEA Agreement, in force since 1 January 1994, extends the single market's rules on goods, services, capital and labour — together with competition, state aid, consumer protection, employment and environmental law — to Iceland without giving it a vote on any of them. This is the arrangement usually described from inside the Union as rule-taking.

Outside the EEA's reach: the common agricultural and fisheries policies, the customs union and common external tariff, the common commercial policy, monetary union, and justice and home affairs beyond what Schengen covers.

Schengen has applied since 2001, so border checks with the Union are gone even though the border itself is a customs border. Iceland is a member of EFTA and disputes under the EEA go to the EFTA Court rather than the Court of Justice of the EU.
Detailed legal analysis — how much of the acquis actually applies, and how EEA law is incorporated domestically — is pending.

legal.title: Rule of law
legal.sub: World Bank governance estimate, roughly −2.5 to +2.5. Aggregated from expert assessments and surveys — perceptions of governance, not a count of legal facts. Both of these countries sit near the top of this scale throughout, which is the headroom problem the governance estimates run into everywhere in this project.

financial.title: Financial
paras: The same World Bank series collected for every member state. Two charts that appear on member pages are absent here and cannot be filled in: EU budget flows, because a non-member neither pays into the budget nor receives from it, and the Eurostat long-term bond series, which is a euro-convergence indicator collected for member states only.

charts.title: GNI per capita, PPP vs the EU average
charts.sub: Current international $. The EU aggregate is available from 1996.

charts.title: Real income per head, % of the EU average
charts.sub: Constant 2015 US$, so this one is not moved by exchange rates or inflation — useful as a cross-check on the headline chart.

commercial.title: Commercial
paras: Trade openness is the outcome this project can establish causally for EU members, and it is also the one where the EEA does most of its work: these countries are inside the single market for goods and services without being inside the Union. Read these lines as the counterfactual the trade estimate is measured against.

commercial.title: Trade in goods & services, % of GDP
commercial.sub: Exports and imports of goods and services.

commercial.title: Who it trades with: the EU's share
commercial.sub: Share of total exports going to the EU. Coverage for non-EU reporters in the Eurostat dataset begins around 2013, so this is two observations rather than a series — but the level is the point. Non-members are not trading elsewhere; they are trading with the Union, from outside it.

charts.title: International arrivals, millions
charts.sub: World Bank / UNWTO border arrivals. Series generally ends 2019–2020.

political.title: Political
paras: The verified timeline is on the Overview tab. Applied in 2009 after the banking collapse, suspended talks in 2013, and holds an advisory referendum on resuming them on 29 August 2026.

The political question here is the mirror of the one every member page asks. A member page asks what joining did. This one asks what staying out did — and that is a counterfactual about a country that never entered, which no comparison of observed outcomes can supply. See the panel at the top of the Overview tab.

charts.title: Voice and accountability
charts.sub: World Bank governance estimate, roughly −2.5 to +2.5. Aggregated from expert assessments and surveys — perceptions of governance, not a count of legal facts.

charts.title: Control of corruption
charts.sub: World Bank governance estimate, roughly −2.5 to +2.5. Aggregated from expert assessments and surveys — perceptions of governance, not a count of legal facts. Higher is better.

social.title: Social
paras: Free movement of people applies here through the EEA and Schengen exactly as it does inside the Union, so the migration series is not measuring a difference in regime.

social.title: Net migration, thousands of people
social.sub: UN World Population Prospects estimates via World Bank. Blue = net inflow, red = net outflow.

charts.title: Income inequality (Gini index)
charts.sub: World Bank estimate (0 = perfect equality). Survey-based, so gaps mean no survey rather than no change.

charts.title: Net migration per 1,000 residents
charts.sub: The same flow scaled by population, which is the comparable form.

sources.label: Time series
sources.text: World Bank Open Data (api.worldbank.org). Indicator codes travel with every value in data/indicators.csv.

sources.label: Milestones
sources.text: Statistics Norway, the Norwegian Government, the Council of the EU, the European Commission (DG NEAR), EFTA, Iceland's National Electoral Commission and RÚV. The source for each row is recorded in data/milestones.csv, and where two credited sources disagree the row says so rather than picking one.

sources.label: Relationship metadata
sources.text: EEA, Schengen and EFTA status in data/nonmembers.csv.

method.title: Why this page exists
method.text: Iceland is one of the non-member countries every estimate in this project is measured against. A control group that is never shown is a control group nobody can check.

method.title: What is missing, and why
method.text: EU budget flows and the Eurostat bond series are absent because they do not exist for a non-member — not because collection failed. Everything else on a member page is here.

method.title: The EEA changes what the comparison means
method.text: Both non-member profiles in this set are inside the single market through the EEA. So the contrast with a member state is not integration against isolation; it is integration without membership against integration with it. That makes them a demanding control, and it is one reason the trade estimate for the Western bloc does not survive its checks.

method.title: Attribution caution
method.text: Nothing on this page shows what not joining caused. That would need a counterfactual for a country that never entered, which this design cannot produce.
